claims.text: The starting MoNbTaW refractory HEA is a homogeneous solid solution with a uniform microstructure.
A minor Zr addition followed by aging at approximately 900 °C will induce nanoscale precipitation in MoNbTaW.
The precipitates induced by Zr addition and aging will be Zr-based carbides or borides.
The Zr-based carbide or boride precipitates will be fine, coherent, and uniformly dispersed in the refractory HEA matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion through dispersion strengthening.
Interfaces associated with the precipitates will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
The precipitates will be chemically inert.
The chemical inertness of the precipitates will minimize their coarsening at high temperature.
Suppressed precipitate coarsening will maintain the alloy's thermal stability.
The Zr-added and aged alloy will have higher yield strength than homogeneous, as-synthesized MoNbTaW without Zr.
The Zr-added and aged alloy will have improved ductility relative to homogeneous, as-synthesized MoNbTaW without Zr.
The Zr-added and aged alloy will have enhanced resistance to irradiation-induced damage relative to homogeneous, as-synthesized MoNbTaW without Zr.
The Zr-added and aged alloy will preserve high-temperature stability.
Overaging or excessive precipitate coarsening may diminish mechanical performance or thermal stability.
Minor compositional variations can alter phase equilibria and precipitation kinetics.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies adding only Zr to MoNbTaW, but the proposed mediator consists of carbides or borides; no carbon or boron source, concentration, or pre-existing content is specified. Formation of the named phases therefore does not follow compositionally from the stated intervention.
